preamble: Before front vowels and /j/, the glottal fricative /h/ acquires a tongue-body constriction and can surface as, or merge with, the alveolo-palatal fricative [ɕ]. In Asante Twi, /h/ is palatalized to [ɕ] before front vowels (written hy). In traditional Tokyo (Shitamachi) speech and much of Tohoku, /hi/ [çi] merges with /si/ [ɕi], so higashi 'east' is said sigasi. Southern Gyeongsang Korean likewise turns /h/ before /i/ or /j/ into /s/, realized [ɕ] before /i/, as in him > sim 'strength'.

examples.note: Allophonic palatalization of /h/ before front vowels, part of the general Akan palatalization of velars and /h/; orthographic ⟨hy⟩.
Confusion of /hi/ [çi] with /si/ [ɕi]; a stereotypical trait of traditional Shitamachi Tokyo speech, also widespread in Tohoku.
h-palatalization (ㅎ구개음화): /h/ before /i/ or /j/ becomes /s/, which is [ɕ] before /i/; compare dialectal 성 for 형 'older brother'.
